elements.element: Governing law is the law of the State of New York
elements.evidence: "governed exclusively by the laws of the State of New York"

elements.element: Exclusive jurisdiction lies in the state and federal courts in New York County
elements.evidence: "The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction"

elements.element: Forum is genuinely exclusive (no open-ended carve-out to other courts)
elements.evidence: "seeking temporary injunctive relief in those courts"

elements.element: Governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales
elements.evidence: "the laws of the State of New York" — outside the fallback set

elements.element: Forum is Delaware, California, or London courts, corresponding to the chosen law
elements.evidence: "courts located in New York County, New York"

reasons: The Singapore law and forum wording in 28.1 is replaced with New York law, and 28.2's pre-existing exclusive New York County state and federal court forum is left intact, so law and forum form the permitted preferred corresponding pair.

The second edit narrows the injunctive-relief carve-out from "another court with jurisdiction" to "those courts", which is the short phrase change needed to make the preferred exclusive forum genuinely exclusive rather than an additional bargain.
Fallback is not satisfied on its own terms (neither Delaware/California nor England and Wales/London), but that is irrelevant because the locked preferred level is fully met.

No unrelated term is disturbed: the personal-jurisdiction submission, venue waiver, and the confidentiality/IP scope of the interim-relief sentence remain effective and no undefined term or dangling reference is introduced.
